new-neighbor.title: Meeting a new neighbor.
signature: Hello. My name is Omar. What's your name?
I'm Sara. This is my first day in the neighborhood.
Welcome! That is the library across the street.
Is there a place to buy bread nearby?
Yes, there is a bakery next to the library.

cafe-order.title: Ordering at a café.
signature: Good morning. What would you like?
I'd like to order a cup of tea, please.
Would you like some milk with your tea?
No, thank you. Can I have some water as well?
Of course. You don't have to pay until you leave.

find-the-platform.title: Finding the platform.
signature: Excuse me. Do you know where the train leaves from?
It leaves from platform three. This is the way to the platforms.
Do I have to show my ticket here?
You can show it on the train. You need to be there before ten.
Thank you. I think I have enough time.

study-together.title: Planning a study session.
signature: I want to practise English before the exam.
I have to work this afternoon. Can I meet you tomorrow?
Of course. We need to bring our notebooks.
It's worth reviewing the difficult examples first.

a-new-routine.title: An old habit and a new routine.
signature: I used to take the bus to work every day.
How do you get to work now?
I usually walk. It takes twenty minutes to get there.
I managed to walk to work twice this week.
That's a good start. Let's walk together on Monday.

market-budget.title: Shopping on a budget.
signature: How much do these tomatoes cost?
These are three dollars a kilo. Would you like a bag?
I bought a bag yesterday. I only need two kilos today.
Let me weigh them for you.

clinic-desk.title: An appointment at the clinic.
signature: I feel tired, and I need to see a doctor.
I'd like an appointment this afternoon.
There is an appointment at three. You should arrive ten minutes early.

project-meeting.title: Moving a project meeting.
signature: Could you please move the meeting to Thursday?
I think Thursday will work because the team is free.
Let me know if the time changes.
I'll send you a message. We don't have to book a new room.

library-book.title: Borrowing a library book.
signature: Do you know if the library is open today?
Yes. There are two copies of your book on that shelf.
Of course. Could you please show me your library card?

family-weekend.title: A family visit at the weekend.
signature: Would you like to visit our grandparents this weekend?
I used to visit them every Friday. I want to see them again.
Let's take some fruit with us.
It's worth leaving early so we can spend more time with them.

missed-bus.title: After missing the bus.
signature: I missed the bus because of the rain.
Is there another bus stop nearby?
There is one near the school, but it takes ten minutes to walk there.
Let's walk there. I prefer walking to waiting here.

phone-help.title: Help with a flat battery.
signature: I forgot to charge my phone.
Would you like to use my charger?
Thank you. Can I use your phone for a moment?
Of course. Let me show you where to plug in the charger.

meal-plan.title: Planning lunch.
signature: Would you like some rice for lunch?
I prefer soup to rice today.
There are four of us. Let's make enough for everyone.

museum-entrance.title: Finding the museum entrance.
signature: Excuse me, where is the entrance to the museum?
That is the main entrance, just past the garden.
Can I buy a ticket there?
Yes. There is a ticket desk just inside.

shared-table.title: Sharing a table.
signature: Excuse me, do you mind if I sit here?
Not at all. This is the only free seat.
Thanks. Is it okay if I charge my phone here?
Of course. There is an outlet under the table.

lesson-time.title: Confirming the lesson time.
signature: When is the next English lesson?
The class starts at nine tomorrow.
Do you have the room number?
Yes, I have it here. I'll send it to you.

missing-coat.title: A coat left on the bus.
signature: Did you leave your coat on the bus?
I didn't take it with me when I got off.
Do you know where the lost property office is?
Yes. I'll call the office and give them the bus number.

forgot-receipt.title: Returning an item without a receipt.
signature: I'd like to return this bag. I forgot to bring the receipt.
I need a receipt or the order number.
Can I show you the confirmation on my phone?
Yes. Let me check the order number.

bicycle-saturday.title: Fixing a bike on Saturday.
signature: Are you going to use your bike this weekend?
I'm going to repair it first. I need a new tire.
Can you bring the wheel to my place on Saturday?
Yes. If the shop is open, I'll bring a tire too.

quiet-room.title: Asking for a quieter room.
signature: Would you mind lowering the music a little?
Of course. I'm sorry for playing it so loudly.
That's all right. I have an online lesson in five minutes.
I'll use my headphones until your lesson is over.

help-with-boxes.title: Helping with some boxes.
signature: Can you hold the door while I carry this box?
Of course. How many boxes are there?
There are three. I'll carry the small ones first.
Let's leave the heavy one until we're both free.

rainy-picnic.title: A backup plan for the picnic.
signature: Are you going to the park tomorrow?
I might go, but the weather doesn't look good.
If it rains, I'll make lunch at home instead.
Good idea. Let me know if you need anything.

first-day-office.title: Clarifying the first task.
signature: Could you clarify the instructions for my first task?
Please check the names on this list today.
So I have to check the names today. What about the phone numbers?
I'll check the phone numbers tomorrow. You can leave those to me.
Thanks. I don't have to wait to send the list, then.

shoe-size.title: Trying a different shoe size.
signature: Is there a larger size in these shoes?
Yes. I'll bring you the next size up.
Can I try these shoes on?
Of course. There's a bench by the mirror.
These fit much better. I'd like this pair, please.

fruit-for-guests.title: Fruit for the guests.
signature: Six. These are the oranges we bought last week. We need a few more.
Two dollars a kilo. Let's get a kilo and put out the apples too.

card-payment.title: Paying by card.
signature: Yes. Please tap your card here.
Thanks. I need a receipt for this purchase.
Let me print one for you.

bread-before-closing.title: Bread before closing.
signature: Is there any fresh bread left?
There is one loaf left. Would you like me to put it aside?
Yes, please. When is closing time?
The shop closes at six. I'll keep it behind the counter until then.

wrong-size-online.title: The wrong size arrived.
signature: I bought a jacket online, but the one that arrived is too small.
A medium. I didn't order a small. Could you please check the order number?
You're right. I'll arrange an exchange. Let me know if the return label doesn't arrive by email.

charger-included.title: Does it come with a charger.
signature: That's for charging. Both devices use the same kind of cable.
Which one is cheaper? How much is the smaller one?
It's ninety dollars. The larger one is one hundred and ten.
Does the smaller one come with a charger?
Just a cable. I have a compatible charger here if you need one.

parcel-pickup.title: Picking up a parcel.
signature: Excuse me. I'd like to pick up a parcel.
It's for Omar Ali. Here's the pickup code.
Thank you. May I see your ID as well?

printer-quote.title: Getting a printing quote.
signature: How much does it cost to print in black and white?
Ten cents per page. How many pages do you need?
Twenty. Could you please tell me whether I need to bring a USB drive?
You don't have to bring one. Just email us the file and we'll print it for two dollars.

faulty-kettle.title: A kettle that stopped working.
signature: Did you try plugging the kettle into another outlet?
I did, but it still wouldn't turn on. I didn't try opening it.
I'm sorry for the trouble. I'll ask our technician to check it this afternoon.
Thank you. Here's my number. Please call me before replacing anything.

gift-budget.title: Choosing a gift on a budget.
signature: I want a gift for my sister. I can spend fifteen dollars.
Which one would she use more, a notebook or a book?
I usually prefer notebooks to books as gifts, but she reads every night.
Then this short novel might suit her. It costs twelve dollars.

tailor-pickup.title: Picking up a garment.
signature: When is the earliest I can pick up the trousers?
I can finish the hem tomorrow afternoon.
As soon as they're ready, I'll come by.
I'll text you before five. Let me know if you need to come the following morning instead.

bus-stop-directions.title: Directions to the bus stop.
signature: Excuse me, where is the bus stop?
See the building across the road? That is the school.
Should I cross at the lights?
Yes. There is a bus stop just past the school gate.

direct-airport-train.title: A direct train to the airport.
signature: Are there any direct trains to the airport?
Yes. The next one leaves at seven.
Does it leave from this platform?
No. You have to go to platform three, but you stay on that train all the way.

seat-on-train.title: A seat on the train.
signature: Are there any free seats in this carriage?
There are two by the window.
Can I put my bag on the rack?
Sure. Do you mind if I take the window seat?
Not at all. I'll take the aisle seat.

hotel-checkin.title: Checking in at the hotel.
signature: Good evening. My name is Omar Ali, and I have a reservation.
Welcome. May I see your passport, please?
Of course. Where is the elevator?
Just past the lobby on your right. Your room is on the second floor.

bus-or-walk.title: Taking the bus or walking.
signature: How much is the bus fare?
Two dollars. It takes ten minutes to get there by bus.
I prefer walking to taking the bus if we have time.
We've got half an hour. Let's walk along the river.

wrong-gate.title: A gate change.
signature: Is there a departure screen near here?
There's one by the stairs. Do you know where your flight is boarding?
I didn't see the gate change on my phone. It still says twelve.
They changed the gate, so you need to go to twenty. It's just down this hall.

two-tickets.title: Two ferry tickets.
signature: I'd like two tickets for the ferry, please.
Tomorrow. I want seats together if possible. How much are the tickets?
Eight dollars each. I have two seats together by the window.
The ferry leaves at noon tomorrow.

calling-a-driver.title: Arranging a pickup.
signature: It's outside the main entrance. Could you please wait near the blue sign?
Sure. I'm meeting my brother at the airport at six, so I need to leave by five.
When I get there, I'll call you. I should be at the sign by five.

map-without-signal.title: Using a map without a signal.
signature: I can't load the map. There's no signal here.
I can explain the route without a map. We turn left at the next crossing.
Let me write that down before we move.
If we see the library, I'll know we're on the right road.

bag-at-station.title: A bag at the station.
signature: I've got a blue bag with a gray strap.
This is the one we found near the platform. Does it look familiar?
Yes. The bag that I left has a name tag inside. Could you check it?
It says Omar Ali. You can take it now.

delay-announcement.title: Understanding a delay announcement.
signature: Could you clarify what the announcement said?
The train is delayed because of a signal problem.
Could you tell me whether my ticket is valid on the next train?
Yes. This train won't run, so we'll accept your ticket on the next one.

early-alarm.title: An early alarm.
signature: I wake up at six. What time does your alarm go off?
At six too, but I get up as soon as it rings.
I usually stay in bed for ten more minutes.
I take the bus to work every day, so I can't do that.

before-school.title: Before leaving for school.
signature: What do you do first in the morning?
I brush my teeth first. Then I get dressed.
Do you eat at home or on the way to school?
I have breakfast at home. Before I leave, I check my bag.

after-work.title: After work.
signature: What do you do after work?
After I finish work, I go home and change clothes.
Do you stay home for the rest of the evening?
I sometimes go for a walk. On Thursdays, I go to the library.

weekend-sport.title: Weekend exercise.
signature: On weekends, I often run before breakfast.
Why do you go so early?
It's quieter. I never run at noon because the park is too hot.

night-routine.title: Getting ready for bed.
signature: What do you do at night before bed?
I always set my alarm first. Then I read a little.
Do you finish the book in one evening?
No. It's usually quiet by nine, so I go to bed then.

breakfast-choices.title: Choosing breakfast.
signature: Would you like eggs or oatmeal for breakfast?
I like eggs, but I don't like oatmeal.
Do you want any fruit with the eggs?
Yes, please. I eat an apple most mornings.

find-the-key.title: Looking for the key.
signature: Where is the key to the front door?
I saw it beside your notebook this morning.
I've got the notebook here, but the key isn't under it.
Wait. That is your key on the hook by the door.

lend-a-pen.title: Borrowing a pen.
signature: Do you have a pen I could use?
Yes, I have a spare blue one.
Can I borrow it to fill in this form?
Thank you. I'll give it back in a minute.

window-or-fan.title: The window or the fan.
signature: Is it okay if I open the window? It's warm in here.
I think the street is too noisy. Would you mind turning on the fan instead?
That's fine. I prefer a little noise from the fan to the traffic outside.
Great. The low setting should be enough.

dinner-ingredients.title: Ingredients for dinner.
signature: How many people are we cooking for?
Six. There are four potatoes in the cupboard.
I need two more for the soup.
Let's get a small bag of potatoes and use the rest tomorrow.

first-aid-supplies.title: First-aid supplies.
signature: What is in that small red bag?
Just a few supplies for the class.
Where is the first-aid kit, then?
There is one in the cupboard by the door.
Could you please bring it to the desk?

class-introduction.title: Introductions on the first day.
signature: Hi. My name is Omar. What's your name?
I'm Sara. I'm a new student here.
So am I. Who is the woman by the board?
That's our English teacher. Class is about to start.

repeat-instructions.title: Asking for instructions again.
signature: Could you please repeat the last instruction?
Sure. Write two examples, then exchange your paper with a partner.
Could you clarify which part we check for each other?
Let me show you. Check that the verb comes after the subject.
Thank you for showing me. I'll check the word order first.

quiet-study-place.title: Finding a place to study.
signature: I need a quiet place to study. Is there a library near campus?
Yes. There is a small library behind the main building.
Where do you usually study there?
On the second floor. It's quieter than the entrance hall.

group-presentation.title: Dividing up a presentation.
signature: I can make the slides, but I can't stay late to rehearse.
I can do the introduction. We still need someone for the conclusion.
I must leave by four, but I can write a short conclusion now.
Good. Let's rehearse the whole presentation at three.

teacher-office-hours.title: Meeting the teacher.
signature: May I come by to ask about my essay?
Of course. My office hours are on Tuesdays.
When is the first slot on Tuesday?
At ten, but I'm meeting another student then. I can see you at eleven.
I'm afraid I can't come at eleven. Would noon work?
Yes. Bring your draft and we'll go through it together.

report-deadline.title: The report deadline.
signature: The first draft is due on Friday. The final version is due next week.
So I have to finish the draft this week. Could you please send me the checklist?
I'll send it now. You don't have to add the charts until the final version.

book-recommendation.title: Recommending a book.
signature: I'm interested in hiking. Do you know any books for beginners?
The book that I borrowed last week has some easy routes.
Does it tell you what to bring?
Yes. It lists useful items such as a torch and a map. It's worth reading before your first trip.

practice-club.title: An English practice club.
signature: Would you like to join our English practice club?
I'd love to. What do you do at the meetings?
I usually bring a short dialogue. This week I'm planning to practise ordering food.
How about taking turns as the customer and the server?
Good idea. I'll bring a menu we can use.

online-lesson-audio.title: Trouble hearing the online lesson.
signature: I can't hear you clearly. Could you please repeat the last sentence?
Let me check the microphone. Can you hear me now?
Yes. I didn't catch the first part because the sound cut out.
I'll start the sentence again and write it in the chat too.

exam-mistake.title: Understanding a test mistake.
signature: Did you see why you lost a point on question three?
I didn't understand what it meant by “give one reason.”
What I mean is that you gave an example, but you didn't say why it mattered.
I see. I should have explained the reason in a full sentence.

study-methods.title: Choosing a study method.
signature: How do you remember the phrases you learn?
I prefer saying them aloud to copying them out.
In my opinion, it helps to hide the text first.
Exactly. For example, I look at a picture, say a sentence, and then check the original.

last-shift.title: What happened on the last shift.
signature: Were you at reception when the delivery arrived?
I was in the back office. I was checking the order list.
When the driver arrived, Noor signed for them and called me.

missed-message.title: A missed message.
signature: Did you get my message about the meeting?
I didn't see it. While I was helping a customer, my phone was in a drawer.
We moved the meeting to tomorrow morning.
I'm sorry for missing the update. I'll check my messages at lunch next time.
That's all right. You still have time to read the notes.

old-and-new-job.title: From the old job to the new one.
signature: I used to work in a small shop near my house.
How did you find your new job?
I went to a careers fair and I met the manager of a hotel there.
No. I started working there the following month.

equipment-repair.title: Repairing equipment.
signature: Did you find out why the printer kept jamming?
Yes. I decided to check the back because the front tray was clear.
Was there any paper stuck back there?
A torn sheet was stuck inside, so I removed it with the power off. I managed to print a test page afterwards.

welcoming-intern.title: Welcoming an intern.
signature: This is Sara, our new intern.
Hi. I'm here for two weeks. Who is in charge of the schedule?
Lina is the person who plans the shifts. She sits by the window.
Thanks. I'll go and introduce myself.

new-procedure.title: A new office procedure.
signature: Please save each order as a PDF before you send it.
Could you clarify where to save the file?
Use the shared folder so that the whole team can find it.
Should I put the date in the file name?
Yes. Add the date to make older orders easier to find.

meeting-followup.title: Following up after a meeting.
signature: Will you send everyone the meeting notes?
Yes. I'll send them before lunch. Could you check the dates?
Of course. As soon as I check them, I'll message you.
Thanks. Let me know if any of the deadlines have changed.

safety-check.title: Checking equipment before use.
signature: I must check the guard before I switch the machine on, right?
Yes. And you should keep the checklist where you can see it.
Do I need to print a new copy every day?
You don't have to print another copy unless the instructions change.
Understood. I won't start the machine if the guard is loose.

workshop-choices.title: Choosing a workshop.
signature: I think we should choose the afternoon workshop.
I don't agree with that suggestion. Half the team is on shift then.
Fair point. What matters is that everyone can attend.
I agree with you on that. Let's ask for a morning session next week.

new-deadline.title: Negotiating a new deadline.
signature: Can you send me the report by Thursday?
I might need another day. I expect to finish the figures by Thursday afternoon.
Friday is fine, but I need the summary before the meeting at ten.
If I get the figures early, I'll send the summary on Thursday evening.

launch-feedback.title: Feedback after a launch.
signature: How do you feel about the first week of the new service?
I'm happy with the response. I'm surprised that so many people used it on the first day.
I'm disappointed that we had to turn some people away. The waiting area was full.
I agree. I appreciate your suggestion to offer more appointments next week.

tea-with-a-guest.title: Offering tea to a guest.
signature: Would you like tea or coffee?
I'd like a cup of tea, please. I like it without sugar.
Here you are. It's hot, so be careful.
Thank you for making it. It smells lovely.
You're welcome. Please help yourself to a biscuit.

visiting-grandmother.title: Visiting Grandma.
signature: Are you going to visit Grandma on Saturday?
Yes. I'm going to take her some lunch. What time is the first bus?
The bus leaves at seven in the morning, but there's another at nine.
I'll take the nine o'clock bus.
Great. I'll call Grandma and tell her when to expect you.

changing-a-visit.title: Rescheduling a visit.
signature: Are we still on for this afternoon?
I'm afraid I can't make it. I'm sorry for changing the plan at the last minute.
That's all right. We can meet tomorrow.
I'm not going to be home tomorrow morning. How about coming after lunch?
That works. See you at two.

joining-the-group.title: Joining the group.
signature: Do you mind if I join your group?
Not at all. You may sit here. We're planning a walk on Saturday.
That sounds fun. Where will you meet?
At the park gate. Would you like to come with us?
I'd love to. What time should I be there?

a-friend-feels-tired.title: A friend feels tired.
signature: I feel tired. I'm worried about getting everything done before dinner.
Which task is most urgent? I can help with the others.
The shopping can wait. I should take a short break before I finish the report.

family-memory.title: Remembering a family day.
signature: These are the photos from Grandma's party.
I remember the day when we all surprised her. I had the camera ready by the door.
When she walked in, everyone started clapping.
And I made the cake you can see in this photo. She asked for another slice.

finding-the-playground.title: Finding a place to play.
signature: Where is the playground near the library?
It's the place where we met after class last week. That is the entrance across the road.
Yes, two. Let's cross at the lights and walk in together.

friend-s-new-hobby.title: A friend’s new hobby.
signature: What do you do in your free time these days?
I'm interested in photography. I've been practising in the park.
The photos you sent are lovely. I'm proud of how much you've improved.
Thanks. I hope to put together a small album by the end of the month.

shared-celebration.title: Preparing a celebration.
signature: Would you like to have dinner out for your birthday?
I don't feel like going out. I don't like crowded restaurants on Fridays.
How about making dinner at home instead of eating out?
That sounds good. I feel like making a pizza, and we can invite a few friends.

thank-you-for-help.title: Thanking a helpful neighbor.
signature: Thank you for helping me carry those boxes upstairs.
You're welcome. I'm glad I got home in time to help.
I'm grateful for your help. I wouldn't have managed the big box alone.
It was no trouble. I appreciate you lending me your cart last week, too.

keeping-the-plan.title: Keeping the plan.
signature: I may get there late if the bus is delayed again.
Even if you're late, we'll still have time for the walk.
Although the path might be wet, I'd still like to go.
Me too. I'll probably bring a spare pair of socks, just in case.

office-signup.title: Signing up for a workshop.
signature: I'd like to sign up for the Saturday workshop.
Sure. Do you have an account on our website?
Not yet. May I register here instead?
Yes, just fill in this form.
Thanks. When is the deadline to hand it in?
Five o'clock today. You can leave it with me when you're done.

community-room.title: Booking a community room.
signature: I wonder if the community room is free on Friday evening.
It is, but someone has asked to use it until five.
I wonder how we can book it for six. Could you tell me whether we need to pay in advance?
No payment is due until the day. Fill in this form, and let me know if you need the chairs set out before six.

team-options.title: Choosing a project solution.
signature: I believe a short online form is the quickest way to collect feedback.
I don't agree with using an online form alone. Some visitors don't have internet access.
Printing separate forms would take more time. However, we could leave one tablet at reception.
Good idea. In addition to the tablet, let's keep a few paper copies for anyone who needs one.

testing-assumptions.title: Testing an assumption.
signature: Why is the printer so slow? It seems like the network is down again.
It sounds like a network problem, but let's try printing a test page without the network first.
The test page is slow too. The reason is that the printer is set to its highest quality.
That's why it took so long. Let's use the standard setting for these drafts.

supporting-a-claim.title: Supporting a claim with examples.
signature: In my opinion, we should give new staff a short checklist for their first week.
Routine tasks such as booking a room and sending a receipt. For example, a new starter could use it to see who approves a booking.
That would not only save time but also reduce mistakes. Let's try it with the next group.

competing-priorities.title: Balancing competing priorities.
signature: While a quick release would help customers today, a full review would catch more errors.
Even though the draft looks good, we haven't checked the prices yet.
What matters is that people see the correct prices.
Then let's check the price list now instead of publishing the whole page immediately.

before-the-departure.title: What happened before departure.
signature: I heard you nearly missed the train. What happened?
I had already packed my bag before my ride arrived. But I wasn't ready to leave because I couldn't find my ticket.
Did you find it in time?
Yes, in my jacket. By the time we got to the station, boarding had already started.
So how did you make it?
The conductor said, “I'm about to close the doors.” I showed him my ticket just in time.

if-we-had-called.title: If we had called first.
signature: The hall was locked when we arrived. If we had called first, we would have known it was closed.
I'm sorry for assuming it would be open. I should have checked the opening hours.
We could have met at the library instead. It stays open late.
I'll call the hall tomorrow. If it's still closed, we'll book a table at the library.

imagining-a-solution.title: Imagining a different solution.
signature: I wish I could find a quiet room for our study group. The usual room is full.
If I were you, I would ask the librarian about a room upstairs.
Even if there's no room, we could use two small tables near each other.
Good idea. If you ask about the room now, I'll look for tables.

improving-with-practice.title: Getting better with practice.
signature: I keep forgetting new phrases. How much time do you spend reviewing them?
It takes about ten minutes to review five phrases. The more I use them in conversation, the easier they are to remember.
I think I can fit that in after lunch. Could we practise together on Fridays?
Yes. Let's each bring one new situation so that we can use the same phrases in different ways.

food-plan-alternatives.title: Alternatives for guests.
signature: Would you like rice with the soup, or bread?
Rice, please. I don't eat bread unless it's gluten-free.
We've got plenty of rice. In addition to the soup, we can make a salad.
Great. I need two more cucumbers for the salad. I'll get them on my way home.

early-flight-routine.title: Getting ready for an early flight.
signature: I wake up at four tomorrow. Can you set a second alarm?
Of course. I get up as soon as my alarm goes off. I'll knock on your door.
Before I leave, I check my passport and ticket. Will you check yours too?
Yes. I'll leave them next to my bag tonight.

morning-at-the-hotel.title: Breakfast at the hotel.
signature: In the morning, is breakfast served here or upstairs?
Upstairs. The dining room opens at seven.
Great. I have breakfast before my first meeting when I travel.
We can also pack breakfast for you if you leave before seven.

sleepover-toothbrush.title: A toothbrush for a sleepover.
signature: I brush my teeth right after breakfast, but I left my toothbrush at home.
There's a new one in the bathroom cupboard.
Thanks. I always forget something when I pack in a hurry.
Put it next to your bag when you're done so you remember it tomorrow.

evening-reading-habit.title: Reading before bed.
signature: At night, I leave my phone in the kitchen and read.
I often fall asleep after just one page.
I go to bed at ten, but I start reading at half past nine.
That gives you time to enjoy the book. I'll try that.

lunch-on-a-budget.title: Lunch on a budget.
signature: I eat lunch at home most days. Where can we get a cheap lunch here?
I sometimes buy soup at the café by the office. It's four dollars.
I never buy lunch without checking the price first. Four dollars is fine.
Let's go now, before it gets busy.

library-after-class.title: The library after class.
signature: After I finish class, I go to the library. Do you want to come?
I have another class, but I can meet you later. When do you leave the library?
At about four. I study there every day until then.
I'll meet you there at half past three.

cycling-club-weekends.title: A weekend cycling group.
signature: On weekends, our cycling group rides by the river.
Where do you meet before the ride?
At the park gate. I usually arrive a little early.
I'll come on Saturday. I'll bring water and a helmet.

museum-audio-guide.title: Borrowing an audio guide.
signature: What is this device next to the tickets?
It's an audio guide. Can you hear the sample through those headphones?
Yes, clearly. Can I borrow it for the visit?
You may borrow it until closing time. Return it here on your way out.

gym-water-break.title: A water break at the gym.
signature: Is it okay if I stop for a minute? I need some water.
Of course. There is a water fountain by the door.
I feel better already. I should bring my own bottle next time.
Take another minute, then we'll finish with an easy stretch.

laptop-at-reception.title: Leaving a laptop for repair.
signature: I have a laptop that won't charge.
Let me check the charger first. I can test it here.
Thanks. I can't leave the laptop overnight.
You should keep it with you until we know whether the charger is the problem.

appointment-reminder.title: Confirming an appointment.
signature: When is my appointment with the nurse?
It's on Tuesday at half past ten. Please arrive a few minutes early.
I have to bring my ID, right?
Yes. You don't have to print the confirmation. You can show it on your phone.

tea-at-reception.title: Tea at reception.
signature: Would you like some tea while you wait?
I'd like a cup, please. I don't like sugar in my tea.
Thanks. I'll drink it here before the meeting.

finding-the-host.title: Finding the host.
signature: Who is the host of this event?
That is the host by the door. Where is your guest badge?
It's in my pocket. My name is Omar, by the way.
Nice to meet you. What's your friend's name? I'll look for her badge too.

coffee-machine-queue.title: At the office coffee machine.
signature: Why is the machine so quiet? Is it off?
It's out of water. How do you open the tank?
Lift this handle. This is the part you fill.
Now I see. Let's fill it before the next person comes.

new-flat-tour.title: A tour of a new flat.
signature: How is the new flat? Is it big enough?
Yes. There is a small balcony, and there are two bedrooms.
These are your new keys, right?
Yes. The round one opens the main door.

choosing-a-course.title: Choosing an evening course.
signature: What do you look for in an evening class?
Do you mean the subject or the timetable?
Both. Why do you prefer the smaller class?
I get more time to speak. Which one would you choose?

bakery-two-loaves.title: Buying two loaves.
signature: Is there any wholemeal bread left?
Yes. How many loaves would you like?
Two, please. How much is each loaf?
Three dollars. I like this one toasted, if you'd like to try it that way.

group-bus-booking.title: Booking seats for a group.
signature: Are there six seats together on the afternoon bus?
There are four together and two across the aisle.
Does the bus stop near the town hall?
Yes. The driver can tell you when you get there.

old-school-reunion.title: A school reunion.
signature: Were you in Ms Green's class in our last year?
No. I wasn't in that class. I was in the room next door.
Oh, right. I had a friend from your class. His name was Sam.
I remember him. He always brought a sketchbook.

market-festival-story.title: A story from the festival market.
signature: I went to the festival market on Saturday.
Did you find the pottery stall?
Yes. I saw a blue bowl I liked, and I met the woman who made it.
I bought a cup from her last year. Is she still near the entrance?

forgotten-birthday-card.title: A forgotten birthday card.
signature: I forgot to buy a birthday card. Do we have any thick paper?
Yes. I made a card with this paper last week.
Good idea. I decided to make the gift myself, so I can make the card too.
I'll cut the paper while you write the message.

rain-at-the-market.title: Sudden rain at the market.
signature: While I was looking for fruit, it started to rain.
I didn't see any clouds when we left home.
I was waiting under a shop awning for ten minutes.
When the rain stopped, I went back for the vegetables.

community-garden-start.title: Starting a community garden.
signature: I used to grow tomatoes on my balcony.
What made you join the community garden?
I started helping a neighbour there last spring.
I managed to grow my first peppers there too. I'd be happy to show you.

borrowed-bike-return.title: Returning a borrowed bike.
signature: Will you bring the bike back before dinner?
Yes. I'll leave it next to the front door at six.
I won't leave it unlocked. I'll text you when it's there.

saturday-train-plans.title: Saturday train plans.
signature: Are you going to drive to the coast on Saturday?
No. I'm not going to drive there. The roads get busy.
I'm going to take the train too. Shall we book together?
Yes. I'm planning to return in the evening. Does that work for you?

airport-pickup-time.title: An airport pickup time.
signature: I'm meeting my cousin at the airport at six.
No. I expect to hear from him once he lands.
When you hear from him, I'll check the traffic for you.

weather-for-the-fair.title: Weather for the fair.
signature: I may bring an umbrella to the fair tomorrow.
I'll probably wear a light jacket too.
I might arrive late if the rain is heavy.
No problem. If it rains, I'll wait by the covered entrance.

deliver-before-closing.title: Delivery before closing.
signature: I'm about to leave the shop. Has the driver called?
Not yet. As soon as he calls, I'll text you.
Thanks. I hope to get the parcel before the shop closes.
I'll ask him to leave it at reception if you've gone.

first-interview-introduction.title: Introducing yourself in an interview.
signature: Good morning. My name is Omar Ali. I'm here for the interview.
Welcome, Omar. What do you do at the moment?
I'm a shop assistant. I have two years of experience with customers.
Thank you. Could you tell me about a busy day at your shop?

why-this-job.title: Why you want this job.
signature: Why do you want to work here?
I'm interested in helping customers solve problems.
What would you like to learn in this role?
I want to learn how to handle customer requests by phone as well as in person.

interview-strength.title: Explaining a strength in an interview.
signature: What is one of your strengths?
I can explain a difficult task in simple steps.
Could you give me an example?
Last month, I managed to teach three new colleagues how to use our booking system.

interview-work-sample.title: Showing a work sample.
signature: May I show you a work sample?
I made this checklist to help new staff handle returns.
It's clear. How did you decide what to include?

interview-work-schedule.title: Discussing work hours in an interview.
signature: When do you need someone to start?
Next Monday. Do you work weekends at your current job?
Yes, on Saturdays. I'd like to know which shifts are available here.
We have an early and a late shift. The early shift starts at eight.

interview-learning-gap.title: A skill you are still learning.
signature: Have you used this scheduling software before?
I didn't use it in my last job. I started learning it last week.
I create a test schedule so that I can try each feature before using it at work.

interview-team-story.title: A teamwork story in an interview.
signature: Tell me about a time when your team disagreed.
While I was preparing the schedule, two colleagues asked for the same day off.
While one could change their date, the other couldn't. We agreed to swap a different shift.

interview-feedback.title: Learning from feedback at work.
signature: Tell me about a mistake you learned from.
I sent a draft too early. I should have checked the figures first.
What would you do differently now?
If I had asked a colleague to review it, I would have caught the mistake. I now ask for a second check.

interview-training-question.title: Asking about training in an interview.
signature: Do you have any questions for us?
Could you tell me whether new staff get training on the first day?
Yes. You'll spend the morning with a colleague at reception.
Thanks. Could you clarify how long the rest of the training lasts?

interview-portfolio-link.title: Sending a portfolio after an interview.
signature: Thank you for taking the time to meet me today.
You're welcome. Could you send us the sample you showed?
I'll send the link this afternoon. Let me know if it doesn't open.
Of course. We'll be in touch next week.

interview-handling-pressure.title: Handling pressure at work.
signature: What would you do if several orders arrived at once?
What matters is which orders are urgent. I'd check the deadlines first.
And if two are due at the same time?
If I were the only person on shift, I would ask the supervisor to help me choose.

interview-customer-complaint.title: Resolving a customer complaint.
signature: How did you handle a difficult customer request?
One customer received the wrong size. I said, “I'm sorry for the mix-up.”
The correct size was in stock, so I arranged an exchange that afternoon.

replacement-key-cut.title: Getting a spare key cut.
signature: I want a spare key for the front door. Can you copy this one?
Yes. It takes about five minutes to make a copy.
Great. I've got the original right here.
Thanks. Keep the copy on a different key ring so you can tell them apart.

charging-before-the-trip.title: Charging a phone before the trip.
signature: I need to charge my phone before we leave.
There's a socket near the waiting area.
Do you know where the waiting area is?
Yes, beside the stairs. I'll show you.

short-walk-instead.title: A short walk instead.
signature: Would you like to go to the sports centre?
I don't feel like exercising indoors today.
How about walking by the river instead of going to the centre?
Good idea. I feel like getting some fresh air.

repair-or-replace-bag.title: Repairing or replacing a bag.
signature: The zip on my bag has broken. Should I buy a new bag?
I think it's worth repairing. The rest of the bag is fine.
I prefer repairing things to replacing them, but is it expensive?
A new zip costs less than a new bag. Let's ask the repair shop.

document-before-lockup.title: Submitting a document before closing.
signature: I must hand in this form before the office closes.
Excuse me, are you looking for the submission desk?
Yes. Could you please point me in the right direction?
It's the first door on your left. The office is open for another hour.

quieter-carriage.title: A quieter train carriage.
signature: Do you mind if I sit by the window?
Not at all. Would you mind moving your bag off the aisle seat?
Of course. I'm sorry for leaving it there.
That's all right. There's plenty of room above us.

accepting-a-visit.title: Accepting an invitation to visit.
signature: Would you like to visit my family on Friday?
I'd love to come, but I'm afraid I can't stay for dinner.
That's fine. We can have tea earlier.
Perfect. I'll come at four and bring some fruit.

study-progress-news.title: Sharing news about your progress.
signature: I'm happy with my speaking score this week.
I'm proud of the work you put into it.
I'm surprised that I answered without looking at my notes.
You practised with different questions. Keep doing that.

practice-test-concern.title: A concern after a practice test.
signature: I'm worried about the listening part of the exam.
What was hard about the practice test?
I'm disappointed that I missed both times in the announcement.
Let's practise writing down times first, then try another announcement.

returning-a-neighbors-tools.title: Returning a neighbour's tools.
signature: Here's your toolbox. I'm grateful for your help with the shelves.
You're welcome. Did the brackets fit?
Yes. I appreciate you labelling the screws for me.
Glad it helped. Keep the spare screws in case you need them.

club-location-decision.title: Choosing a venue for the club.
signature: In my opinion, the library would be the easiest place to meet.
I don't agree with that choice for this week. The study rooms are closed.
I believe the community hall is free. Shall I check?
I agree with that plan. We can meet there if it's available.

a-noisy-vent.title: A noisy air vent.
signature: It seems like the noise is coming from the vent above the door.
It sounds like something is loose in there.
The reason is that the cover isn't sitting flat. Can we ask maintenance to look at it?
Yes. I'll report it and ask for another room for this meeting.

cancelled-outdoor-class.title: A cancelled outdoor class.
signature: Why are we meeting in the hall today?
The field is closed because of the rain.
I saw water by the gate. That's why the caretaker put up the sign.
Right. We can still practise indoors because the hall is free.

small-shop-big-order.title: A large order at a small shop.
signature: Although this shop is small, it can prepare our order in one day.
Even though the other shop is bigger, it asked for three days.
The small shop costs a little more. However, we need the order tomorrow.
Let's order from here, but check that delivery is included.

welcome-pack-ideas.title: Planning a welcome pack.
signature: What should go into the welcome pack for new staff?
Practical things such as a map of the building and a list of key contacts.
In addition to those, we could add short answers to common questions. For example, where should visitors wait?
That would not only help new staff but also save time at reception.

outdoor-event-backup.title: A backup for an outdoor event.
signature: We can keep the tables outside unless it starts to rain.
Even if it stays dry, some guests will need shade.
What I mean is that we can use both areas and let guests choose.
Good. What matters is that everyone has somewhere comfortable to sit.

finding-a-bike-locker.title: Finding a bike locker.
signature: I wonder if the station has lockers for bikes.
I saw some by the side entrance yesterday.
I wonder how you reserve one.
There's a code on the sign. It opens the booking page.

returning-the-library-book.title: Returning a library book.
signature: Where do I return the book that I borrowed last week?
Give it to the person who is sitting at the front desk.
Is that the place where we signed up for our cards?

first-club-session-memory.title: Remembering the first club session.
signature: Do you remember the day when we started the reading club?
Yes. I had already put out the chairs before anyone arrived.
By the time I got there, the first discussion had started.
We started early because the room was full. I can still remember the first book.

missed-exhibition-opening.title: Missing an exhibition opening.
signature: I wish I could have seen the opening last night.
What stopped you from getting there?
My bus was late. I could have walked from the office, but I thought the bus would be quicker.
The exhibition is open all week. Let's go on Thursday.

listening-speed-progress.title: Progress with gradual listening practice.
signature: Fast conversations are hard for me to follow.
Try a short clip at a comfortable speed first.
The more I replay one section, the easier it gets to hear the words.
Exactly. Then try the same clip again at normal speed.

leave-a-voicemail.title: Leaving a voicemail.
signature: Hello, this is Omar from the repair desk. Could you please call me back?
Hi, Omar. I got your message. What did you need?
I need to confirm a time for tomorrow's visit.
Two in the afternoon is fine. I'll be here.

confirming-a-food-order.title: Checking a food order.
signature: Was that one bowl of soup and two salads?
Yes. Can I have the dressing on the side?
Certainly. Would you like any bread with it?

keeping-leftovers.title: Packing away dinner leftovers.
signature: How many containers do we need for the leftovers?
Two. There are enough vegetables for tomorrow as well.
Let's put the soup in the larger one.
I'll label both containers before I put them away.

requesting-a-menu-change.title: Asking for a change to a meal.
signature: I'd like to order the rice bowl. Can I have it without onions?
Yes. We can add extra cucumber.
That sounds good. I don't like raw onions.
I'll make sure the kitchen sees your request.

shared-grocery-list.title: A shared grocery list.
signature: I need a few things from the market. Do we have any rice?
There is a bag in the cupboard. We only need vegetables.
How many tomatoes should I buy?
Four should be enough. Add a lemon to the list, please.

group-book-exchange.title: A neighbourhood book swap.
signature: This is the table for books we want to give away.
Can I bring magazines as well?
Yes. These are the labels for books, magazines and comics.
I'll put mine under the magazine label.

guest-vegetarian-dinner.title: Planning a vegetarian dinner.
signature: Would you like to stay for dinner?
Yes, thanks. I like vegetable dishes, and I don't eat meat.
There are plenty of beans and vegetables.
How about making a bean salad to go with the rice?

dessert-to-take-home.title: Dessert to take home.
signature: I'd like two slices of cake to take home, please.
Which one would you like, lemon or chocolate?
One of each. How much is that altogether?
Six dollars. I'll put them in separate boxes.

washing-up-together.title: Sharing the kitchen clean-up.
signature: After I clear the table, I'll wash the dishes.
I can dry them while you wash.
Thanks. Can you put the cups away first?

reschedule-a-clinic-visit.title: Rescheduling a clinic visit.
signature: I'd like to change my appointment on Monday.
Of course. When is a good time for you?
Thursday morning, if possible. I can't come in the afternoon.
There's a slot at nine. I'll send you a new confirmation.

finding-the-clinic-desk.title: Finding the clinic reception desk.
signature: Excuse me, where is the reception desk?
It's behind the glass doors. Are you here for an appointment?
Yes. I've got the appointment details on my phone.
Show them to the receptionist and take a seat in the waiting area.

help-reading-a-form.title: Getting help with a form.
signature: Could you please help me read this form?
Sure. What is the first box asking for?
My contact number. Could you clarify whether they want my mobile number?
Yes, write the number they can reach you on during the day.

pickup-for-a-friend.title: Picking up a friend after an appointment.
signature: How is your afternoon looking? Can you pick me up after my appointment?
I can. When is your appointment?
At two. As soon as I'm done, I'll text you.
Great. I'll wait outside the main entrance.

temporary-library-card.title: Getting a temporary library card.
signature: Is there a way to borrow books for just one week?
Yes. You may apply for a temporary card.
I need two books for a short course. Can I apply today?
Yes. Fill in this form and I'll activate the card at the desk.

charging-at-the-library.title: A seat near a library socket.
signature: Are there any free seats near a socket?
Yes, there's one behind the shelves.
Is it okay if I charge my laptop there?
Of course. Please keep the cable away from the aisle.

first-group-meeting.title: A first study group meeting.
signature: Where do you want to meet to plan our presentation?
There is a quiet table outside the classroom.
Great. When we meet, I'll bring the draft slides.
And I'll bring our notes so we can check what is missing.

explaining-a-map.title: Explaining a route on a map.
signature: Do you know where the bus stops near the museum?
Yes. This is the museum on the map. The stop is across from it.
How do you get to the stop from here?
Go straight, then turn left at the bakery.

one-bag-overnight.title: Packing for one night.
signature: I want a small bag for our overnight trip.
Which one will hold your shoes as well?
I've got an extra pocket in this one.
Use that pocket for your shoes. The rest should fit in the main part.

check-out-at-noon.title: Checking out at noon.
signature: At noon. You don't have to bring the room key down until then.
Can I leave my bag here after I check out?
Yes. We'll keep it at reception until you return.

exchange-train-ticket.title: Exchanging a train ticket.
signature: I have a ticket for the evening train, but I'd like to leave earlier.
Let me check whether your ticket can be changed.
Thank you. How much does the change cost?
There's no fee today. I can move you to the four o'clock train.

airport-meeting-sign.title: A sign for an airport pickup.
signature: I'm meeting a guest I've never seen before at the airport.
How about making a sign with their name?
Good idea. I'll print it to make the name easier to read.
Stand near the arrivals doors so they can see you.

walk-around-the-block.title: A walk around the block.
signature: I walk around the block every day after breakfast.
I often go later, when it's cooler.
Do you want to walk together on Friday?
Yes. I'll meet you at the corner after lunch.

quiet-hours-at-home.title: Agreeing on quiet hours at home.
signature: At night, the sound from the television carries upstairs.
I'm sorry for leaving it so loud.
Would you mind using headphones after nine?
Of course. I'll keep a pair next to the remote.

desk-near-the-window.title: Putting a desk near the window.
signature: I prefer working near the window to working by the door.
Why is that corner better for you?
It's brighter, but the desk might be too wide.
Let's measure it before we move anything.

a-note-for-the-neighbour.title: A note for a neighbour.
signature: I feel like baking something for our new neighbours.
How about making muffins and leaving a note?
Good idea. I'll start with “My name is Omar.”
Yes. You could add that we're next door if they need anything.

plant-watering-while-away.title: Watering plants while someone is away.
signature: Could you please water my plants while I'm away?
Of course. How many pots are on the balcony?
Four. These are the ones that need water on Friday.
Thanks. I'll send you a message after I've watered them.

photo-permission-at-a-fair.title: Asking to take a photo at a fair.
signature: Do you mind if I take a photo of the display?
Not at all. Please keep the flash off.
Thanks. Can I take a photo from this side too?
Yes, just stay behind the rope.

birthday-surprise-timing.title: Timing a birthday surprise.
signature: Are you going to bring the cake before everyone arrives?
Yes. I'm going to leave it in the kitchen until we need it.
If Grandma gets here early, I'll take her into the garden.
Perfect. I'll call you when the candles are ready.

refund-or-exchange.title: A refund or an exchange.
signature: I bought this shirt yesterday, but it's too small.
We can exchange it or give you a refund. Would you like a larger size?
Yes. Which one is the next size up?
This one. You can try it on before you decide.

collecting-a-repaired-phone.title: Collecting a repaired phone.
signature: I'd like to collect my phone. Here's the repair ticket.
Let me find it. We replaced the charging port.
Yes. I'll plug it in here so you can see it working.

office-visitor-badge.title: Getting a visitor badge.
signature: Excuse me, may I have a visitor badge?
Of course. Who is your contact here?
Sara Hassan. I'm meeting her at ten.
I'll let her know you're here. Please wait by the window.

read-back-an-address.title: Reading an address back.
signature: Could you please read the delivery address back to me?
Of course. Seventeen Green Street, second floor.
Thanks. What I mean is that the entrance is on Green Lane, behind that building.
I'll add that note for the driver.

handoff-before-leaving.title: Handing over before leaving.
signature: I'm about to leave. Can I hand over these two requests?
Yes. Did you finish the urgent one?
I did. There is one reply still waiting for approval.
I'll check for approval and send it when it's ready.

asking-for-a-short-extension.title: Asking for a short extension.
signature: I might need another day to check the final numbers.
Can you send me the summary today?
If I finish it by four, I'll send it before I leave.
That works. Please mark the numbers that still need checking.

running-a-remote-meeting.title: Running a remote meeting.
signature: I can't see the document you're sharing.
Let me send you the link in the chat.
Thanks. I'll open it on my phone so that I can follow along.
Great. We're looking at the second page.

introducing-a-new-teammate.title: Introducing a new teammate.
signature: Welcome to the team. My name is Omar, and this is the support desk.
Nice to meet you. Who is on the afternoon shift?
Lina. I'll introduce you when she gets here.
Thanks. I'd like to see how she handles new requests.

interview-arrival-delay.title: Running late for an interview.
signature: I'm sorry for calling so close to the appointment. My bus has been delayed.
Thanks for letting us know. How late do you expect to be?
About ten minutes. May I still come in today?
Yes. Let me know if the delay gets longer.

interview-asking-about-duties.title: Asking about the duties of a role.
signature: You'll answer customer questions and help with bookings.
Could you clarify what I would do when a booking needs to change?
Check what is available, then contact the customer.
Could you tell me whether I need approval before making the change?

interview-first-week-plan.title: A plan for your first week.
signature: What would you do in your first week here?
I hope to learn how the team handles requests.
How would you go about learning that?
I think I'd watch a colleague first, then handle a simple request with their help.

l2-001.title: Finding the right words.
signature: How did your first conversation class go?
I find it difficult to express myself in French.
Let's start with a short voice note. Tell me one thing you did today.

l2-002.title: Choosing your opening words.
signature: I can't put up with this noise anymore.
What do you think I should say?
Start by asking if it's a good time to talk. Then explain what you can hear.

l2-003.title: Apologising for a lost book.
signature: Did you find the book I lent you?
I want to apologize for what I did.
I appreciate that. Tell me where you last had it and we'll look together.

l2-004.title: Living on your own.
signature: When did you start cooking for yourself?
What was the first dish you learned to make?

l2-005.title: Checking the window before leaving.
signature: Can we leave for the station now?
I forgot to close the window.
I'll wait by the lift while you close it.

l2-006.title: An umbrella mix-up.
signature: I couldn't find my umbrella after the meeting.
I'm afraid I took your umbrella by mistake.
That explains it. Could you leave it at reception tomorrow?

l2-007.title: A walk before dinner.
signature: We've got half an hour before dinner.
I feel like going out for a walk.
Good idea. I'll take the shorter route with you.

l2-008.title: Allowing an hour for the station.
signature: Can we leave at nine for the ten o'clock train?
It takes an hour to get to the station.
Then we'd better leave at eight thirty to allow time for the platform.

l2-009.title: Checking when you can leave.
signature: Do I have to stay until the end of the session?
You may leave at any time.
Thanks. I'll step out when my driver arrives.

l2-010.title: Returning a borrowed library book.
signature: I borrowed the book from this library.
The return slot is by the door. Would you like to renew it instead?
Yes, please. I still have two chapters to read.

l2-011.title: Looking forward to another visit.
signature: I had a lovely time today. Shall we meet next month?
I'm looking forward to seeing you again.
I'll send you a couple of dates once I get home.

l2-012.title: Finding a French speaker.
signature: Could someone in your family help me call the hotel in French?
Both of my parents can speak French.
Would either of them have five minutes this evening?

l2-013.title: Working out where the time went.
signature: What slowed you down before the meeting?
Tom kept me waiting for more than 30 minutes.
A lot of time was wasted.
Next time, let's ask everyone to confirm when they're ready.

l2-014.title: Leaving a decision open.
signature: Do you want to buy the desk today?
I have to think about it.
Of course. Take the measurements home and check the space first.

l2-015.title: Meeting on the coast.
signature: Is the coast close enough to walk from here?
It's about three kilometers from here to the coast.
That's fine. Let's leave enough time to get back before dark.

l2-016.title: Thinking about changing jobs.
signature: You asked me to look at your résumé. What's changed?
Let's talk about the kind of work you'd enjoy before we edit it.

l2-017.title: The last person to leave.
signature: I'll stay in the study room for a few more minutes.
Be sure to turn off the light when you leave the room.
I will. I'll lock the door as well.

l2-018.title: Working out how the lock works.
signature: Could you open this locker for me?
I have no idea how it works.
Try turning the knob after entering the code. I can show you.

l2-019.title: Finding someone to help with maths.
signature: Can you help me check these fractions?
Great. Could you show me one example before I try the rest?

l2-020.title: Moving to a quieter room.
signature: There are too many people in this room.
The small room at the end of the corridor is free.
Let's go there so everyone can hear.

l2-021.title: Returning to French practice.
signature: Would you like to join us for a short conversation in French?
It's been a long time since I last spoke French.
We'll start with introductions. You can listen to the first round.
I can still remember a little French.

l2-022.title: Keeping your bedtime routine away from home.
signature: Should I put the toiletries in the suitcase now?
I always brush my teeth before I go to bed.
I'll leave your toothbrush out and pack it in the morning.

l2-023.title: Checking on a friend's plans.
signature: I'm sorry I didn't answer your message. My battery died.
I was worried you wouldn't come.
I'm here now. Did you already order, or shall we look at the menu?

l2-024.title: Asking for more preparation time.
signature: Are you ready to present the draft?
I need a little more time to prepare.
That's fine. Take ten minutes and tell us when you're ready.

l2-025.title: Checking who went on the trip.
signature: Did Tom and Mary take the train to Boston?
Neither Tom nor Mary went to Boston.
Then let's ask who booked the seats before we change the reservation.

l2-026.title: A result you are pleased with.
signature: How do you feel about the final layout?
I'm happy with the way things turned out.
So am I. Shall we send it to the rest of the team?

l2-027.title: A glass of water while waiting.
signature: Would you like something to drink while you wait?
Of course. I'll bring you a glass.

l2-028.title: Wondering about tomorrow's weather.
signature: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.
Let's set a table inside too, in case the weather changes.

l2-029.title: Talking about a place you've never visited.
signature: What was your first trip to the States like?
I have never been to the States.
I must have mixed you up with someone else. Where did you go last year?

l2-030.title: Making time for reading.
signature: How do you finish a book every week?
I spend a lot of time reading.
Could I start with twenty minutes after dinner?

l2-031.title: Correcting yourself in a meeting.
signature: The email says the workshop is on Thursday, not Tuesday.
Thanks for checking. I'll correct the calendar invitation.

l2-032.title: A decision that needs a conversation.
signature: Can we confirm the new schedule today?
I can't make that decision without talking to Tom first.
All right. I'll keep both options open until you've spoken to him.

l2-033.title: A new French practice agreement.
signature: We keep switching to English when the exercises get harder.
From now on, we'll only speak French.
Agreed. If I get stuck, I'll try to explain the word in French.

l2-034.title: Waiting for a reply.
signature: Is there anything else you can send with the application?
All I can do at the moment is wait.
Then let's put a reminder in the calendar for next week.

l2-035.title: When more thinking makes it harder.
signature: Have you worked out what the last question is asking?
The more I think about it, the less I understand it.
Let's try a small example and see what changes.

l2-036.title: Waiting in the right place.
signature: Is this the queue for the reception desk?
I was told to wait here.
You're in the right place. They'll call your name when it's your turn.

l2-037.title: Getting ready to resume work.
signature: Would you like another few minutes before we start?
I'm ready to get back to work.
Great. We'll go through the two remaining requests together.

l2-038.title: Identifying an unfamiliar fruit.
signature: What is this fruit next to the lemons?
It does. Let's ask the seller what it is before we buy it.

l2-039.title: A call as soon as you get home.
signature: The bus is here. I'll head home now.
Call me as soon as you get home.
I will. It should take about twenty minutes.

l2-040.title: Choosing a quiet evening activity.
signature: Shall I put on the television?
I prefer reading books to watching television.
I'll turn it off then. Could you recommend a book?

l2-041.title: Welcoming a visitor.
signature: I made it just before the doors closed.
I'm glad I could make it. Where should I put my coat?

l2-042.title: Handling the important task first.
signature: Could you call the client before lunch? They need to confirm the address.
Since it's important, I'll do it.
Thanks. Let me know if the delivery point has changed.

l2-043.title: Giving credit for an idea.
signature: Whose idea was it to add a map to the welcome pack?
I'm the one who came up with the idea.
Good idea. Could you show the new team how it works?

l2-044.title: A short business trip.
signature: Where did you go for your meeting last week?
I went to Boston for five days on a business trip.
Did you have time to visit the city after the meetings?

l2-045.title: Choosing how to get there.
signature: Would it be easier if you rented a car?
I don't know how to drive a car.
Then let's share a taxi from the station.

l2-046.title: Shopping with priorities.
signature: Do you want to buy everything on this list today?
I don't have enough money to buy everything I need.
Let's get the basics today and leave the rest for next week.

l2-047.title: Returning to a closed shop.
signature: The repair shop has closed early. What will you do?
I plan to come back tomorrow.
I'll check when it opens and send you the time.

l2-048.title: Adjusting an activity for a smaller class.
signature: Half of the students are absent.
Then we can make two groups instead of four.
Good. I'll give each group a different question.

l2-049.title: Encouraging someone to ask.
signature: I'm still getting used to the office.
Don't hesitate to ask if you want anything.
Thanks. Could you show me where the spare stationery is?

l2-050.title: Opening a gift together.
signature: Is it all right if I open this now?
Go ahead and unwrap your gift.
Thank you. I'll open it carefully so I can keep the paper.

l2-051.title: How long have you studied French.
signature: How many years have you been studying French?
I've been studying French for three years.
Then you'll be fine in the conversation group. We meet on Thursdays.
Do I need to understand everything people say?
At this time, you don't need to understand everything.

l2-052.title: Finding a way to wind down.
signature: For some reason, I'm wide awake and can't fall asleep.
Let's move tomorrow's early meeting so you have more time to rest.

l2-053.title: Looking for a flat near work.
signature: I'm looking for an apartment to rent.
Do you want to live near work or near the station?
Near the station, as long as it's on a quiet street.

l2-054.title: Making room for a guest.
signature: The guest room isn't ready yet. Would you prefer to stay at a hotel?
I don't mind sleeping on the couch.
Then I'll bring you a blanket and clear the table beside it.

l2-055.title: Thanking someone for their help.
signature: I left a few notes so you can use the new booking system tomorrow.
I can't tell you how much I appreciate your help.
You're welcome. Call me if you get stuck.

l2-056.title: Remembering an old bridge.
signature: Why is the path here wider than the path on the other side?
At one time, there was a bridge here.
That makes sense. Is there a photo of the bridge anywhere?

l2-057.title: Avoiding the same mistake twice.
signature: Why did you check the address twice before sending the parcel?
I didn't want to make the same mistake twice.
Good idea. Let's add that check to the packing list.

l2-058.title: Getting to know a new colleague.
signature: I'll show you where we keep the meeting notes.
By the way, where are you from?
I'm from Muscat. I moved here last month.

l2-059.title: Talking about work you're proud of.
signature: Which project would you like to tell us about?
Could you choose one example and explain your role in it?

l2-060.title: Making a visitor feel included.
signature: I'll introduce our guest to everyone in French.
Keep in mind that Tom doesn't speak French very well.
Good point. I'll introduce him in English and translate the names of the activities.

l2-061.title: Comparing two cities.
signature: Have you been to Boston or Chicago in the past three weeks?
Yes, I was in both cities last month.
In some ways, Boston is nicer than Chicago.
What did you like most about Boston?

l2-062.title: Offering help with luggage.
signature: I can't carry both bags up these stairs at once.
Let me help you with your suitcases.
Thanks. Could you take the larger one?

l2-063.title: Checking whose office it is.
signature: I left a parcel in your office, beside the blue cabinet.
I didn't say this was my office.
You're right. I'll check the name on the door before I fetch it.

l2-064.title: Trying out a new camera.
signature: Is that the camera you were saving for?
I bought a camera the other day.
Let's try it by the window where there's more light.

l2-065.title: Catching up on unfinished homework.
signature: Can you show me your answers to the homework?
To tell the truth, I didn't do my homework.
You can work through the first two questions now and finish the rest tonight.

l2-066.title: Recommending a favourite book.
signature: I'm thinking of borrowing this novel. Have you read it?
That's one of my favorite books.
Then I'll give it a try. Could you tell me which part you liked?

l2-067.title: Explaining a change of plan.
signature: Did you get to the market this morning?
Because of the rain, I could not go out.
We can go together after it stops.

l2-068.title: Giving directions after a wrong turn.
signature: You arrived from the back street. Did the directions help?
I had a hard time finding his house.
Next time, use the park entrance as a landmark. I'll send you a pin.

l2-069.title: Making an early start a habit.
signature: How do you find time to practise before work?
I make it a rule to get up early in the morning.
I'll try getting up twenty minutes earlier on weekdays.

l2-070.title: Asking someone to speak more clearly.
signature: The gate has changed. You'll need to use the walkway on the left.
Of course. Turn left here and follow the signs for gate eight.

l2-071.title: Walking despite the rain.
signature: Did the rain spoil your afternoon in the park?
Even though it was raining, we decided to take a walk.
Then you must have found a sheltered path. Where did you go?

l2-072.title: A rainbow after the storm.
signature: What did you see as soon as the rain stopped?
No sooner had it stopped raining than a beautiful rainbow appeared.
That's why everyone stepped outside with their cameras.

l2-073.title: Talking about the length of a stay.
signature: Do you plan to stay long?
I intend to stay in Boston for three days.
Then you have time for the museum and a walk by the river.

l2-074.title: Noticing more on each reading.
signature: Why are you reading the same book again?
Every time I read this book, I find something new.
I'll try that with a shorter story and make a note of what I notice.

l2-075.title: Finishing a task earlier than expected.
signature: Did you have enough time to finish the report?
I was able to finish the work earlier than I had expected.
Great. Please show me how you organised your notes.

l2-076.title: Finding lost keys in an unexpected place.
signature: Did you check the coat you wore yesterday?
Where were they? I'll put a small bowl there so we have a regular place for them.

l2-077.title: Falling asleep while listening.
signature: Did you hear the end of the radio interview last night?
I fell asleep while listening to the radio.
I'll send you the recording so you can hear the last part.

l2-078.title: Knowing someone since school.
signature: How long have you known Tom?
I've known Tom since high school.
Then you must have plenty of stories from your school days.

l2-079.title: Whose turn is it to take out the rubbish.
signature: We have to put the bin outside before seven.
It's my turn to take out the trash.
Thanks. I'll bring the empty bin back in the morning.

l2-080.title: Checking if someone is still there.
signature: I'm here, but I was just about to leave.
I was wondering if you were still here.
I can stay for another minute. What do you need?

l2-081.title: Working out a machine's controls.
signature: This is the printer we can use for labels.
Choose the label size first. I'll print one as an example.

l2-082.title: Reporting a question about travel.
signature: What did you ask her about before booking the trip?
I asked her if she had been to Mexico.
What did she say? I'd like some advice before we choose a route.

l2-083.title: Understanding a sentence in a book.
signature: I don't understand what this sentence means.
Which word is causing the problem?
The word after the verb. Can we try a simpler example?

l2-084.title: Looking back on a missed lecture.
signature: The tutor explained that point at yesterday's lecture.
I ought to have attended the lecture.
I've got the notes. Let's go through the section you missed.

l2-085.title: Allowing more time for a repair.
signature: Can the technician finish the repair by lunch?
It'll likely take much longer than you expect.
Then let's keep the spare printer available until tomorrow.

l2-086.title: Finding exactly the right item.
signature: Here is a smaller bag with the same strap.
That's what I was looking for.
Great. Would you like to check that your laptop fits?

l2-087.title: Getting ready for a trip.
signature: Can you join us for coffee this afternoon?
I'm busy getting ready for my trip.
No problem. Send me a message when you're back.

l2-088.title: Getting used to a new neighbourhood.
signature: How are you settling into the new flat?
I'm starting to get used to living here.
Would you like me to show you the nearest shops this weekend?

l2-089.title: Wishing you had studied earlier.
signature: I'm thinking of giving up French because I started late.
I wish I had studied French when I was in high school.
Then let's both join the beginner conversation group.

l2-090.title: Being interrupted just before leaving.
signature: Why did Tom miss the first bus?
Tom was about to leave when Mary knocked on the door.
She probably needed to ask him something. Did he take the next bus?

l2-091.title: Deciding if an item is too expensive.
signature: The larger lamp is sixty dollars.
The smaller one costs thirty-five and takes the same bulb.

l2-092.title: Looking for a lost item at work.
signature: I'll check the meeting room for your notebook.
Let me know if you find anything.
I will. What colour is the cover?

l2-093.title: Someone insists on paying.
signature: Did you split the bill at dinner?
Tom insisted on paying for dinner.
Let's invite him for lunch next week so we can return the favour.

l2-094.title: A final task before closing.
signature: I've printed all the labels. Can I turn the computer off?
There's something else I need you to do.
Of course. What else needs doing before we close?

l2-095.title: Relaying a question about your teacher.
signature: What did Tom want to know after the French lesson?
Tom asked me who my French teacher was.
Tell him her beginner class is on Tuesday if he wants to join.

l2-096.title: Too tired to talk after travelling.
signature: Did you get a chance to ask Tom about his trip?
Tom was too tired to speak.
Let's leave him to rest and ask him tomorrow.

l2-097.title: Talking about how long writing took.
signature: Was the letter hard to finish?
It took me three hours to write the letter.
Next time, we can start from the example we saved.

l2-098.title: Politely changing the subject.
signature: We've already talked about the timetable.
Would you mind if I change subjects?
Not at all. What would you like to talk about?

l2-099.title: Checking how soon a task is due.
signature: Could you upload the form when you have a moment?
Do I have to do it right away?
No. Before the end of the day is fine.

l2-100.title: Borrowing a classmate's notes.
signature: I missed the first half of the lecture yesterday.
Of course. I'll send you a scan this afternoon.

l2-101.title: Asking the way to the station.
signature: Can you tell me how to get to the train station?
Take the first left after the library. The station is at the end of that street.
Thanks. Is it close enough to walk?

l2-102.title: Asking what an abbreviation means.
signature: This label says EC. Have you seen it before?
It can mean different things. Let's check the key at the bottom of the page.

l2-103.title: Choosing a restaurant for dinner.
signature: Have you ever been to that Japanese restaurant on Park Street?
Yes. It's quiet and the menu has several vegetarian dishes.
What time does the restaurant close?
At ten. I'll ask if they have a table at seven.

l2-104.title: Checking the first payday.
signature: I've finished setting up your staff account. Do you have any questions?
On the last working day of the month. The date is on your staff calendar.

l2-105.title: Borrowing a ruler in class.
signature: Certainly. Please put it back in the tray when you're done.
I will. I just need to draw a straight line.

l2-106.title: Agreeing on a pickup time.
signature: When should I come pick you up tomorrow?
My flight lands at four, but I'll need time to get my bag.
I'll be outside at half past four. Text me if the flight is late.

l2-107.title: Asking for an approximate repair price.
signature: We can replace the broken zip instead of selling you a new bag.
About how much will it cost?
Around twelve dollars. I'll confirm the price before we start.

l2-108.title: Heating lunch in the office.
signature: There's a microwave beside the sink.
How long should I microwave this?
Start with one minute, then stir it and check the temperature.

l2-109.title: Meeting again after years apart.
signature: I think the last time we met was at your graduation.
How long has it been since we last met?
Almost five years. Let's sit down and catch up.

l2-110.title: Asking when dinner is served.
signature: Welcome. You can leave your bags in the hall.
What time will dinner be served?
At seven. We've left time for everyone to arrive first.

l2-111.title: Asking to speak in private.
signature: You said you wanted to discuss the schedule. Shall we talk here?
Of course. The small meeting room is free.

l2-112.title: Choosing a way to keep warm.
signature: It's getting cold in here. The heater is already on.
Would you mind closing the window?
Not at all. I'll close it and leave the door open.

l2-113.title: Checking if a message was meant for you.
signature: I saw your note asking me to come by.
Did you want to tell me something?
Yes. I moved tomorrow's meeting to the smaller room.

l2-114.title: Choosing how to pay.
signature: How would you like to pay?
By card, please. Could I have a receipt as well?

l2-115.title: Finding a cash machine.
signature: Yes, there's one next to the station entrance.
Thanks. Does it accept cards from abroad?

l2-116.title: Ordering a drink with a meal.
signature: You've ordered the soup and the sandwich.
What do you want to drink with your meal?
Water, please. No ice, if that's possible.

l2-117.title: Putting the rest of a task off.
signature: We've checked most of the entries, but the last page will take a while.
Can't we wait until tomorrow to finish this?
Yes, the report isn't due until Friday. We'll finish it after lunch tomorrow.

l2-118.title: Checking whether entry is allowed.
signature: I need to collect a folder from this room.
Am I allowed to be in here?
Only with a staff member. Wait here and I'll go in with you.

l2-119.title: Suggesting a different day.
signature: I can't make it on Saturday. I've already promised to help my sister.
Sunday works. Let's meet at the same place at eleven.

l2-120.title: Asking for a concrete example.
signature: Explain a problem you solved and what you learned from it.
Can you give me an example?
You could describe a time when a plan changed and you had to find a new solution.

l2-121.title: Finding the right tone in an interview.
signature: You don't need to memorise an answer word for word.
Name the situation first, then explain what you did.

l2-122.title: Asking someone to introduce you.
signature: Can you introduce me to the girl talking with Tom?
Yes. Her name is Lina and she organises the workshops.
Thanks. I'd like to ask her about the photography session.

l2-123.title: Checking that instructions are understood.
signature: First, save a copy. Then add the date to the new file.
Do you understand what you have to do?
Yes. I'll leave the original as it is and work on the copy.

l2-124.title: Asking where to put your coat.
signature: Come in. Everyone's in the sitting room.
Where should I put my coat?
