On the hook by the door. There's a free one on the left.

l2-125.title: Checking your technique.
signature: Hold the paper here and fold along the dotted line.
Almost. Line up these two corners before you press the fold down.

l2-126.title: Talking about your Saturday morning.
signature: What time do you usually get up on Saturday?
At around eight. On weekdays I get up at six.
Let's have breakfast at nine, then.

l2-127.title: Choosing between two devices.
signature: The smaller tablet is lighter, but the other has a longer battery life.
Which one do you think I should buy?
I'd choose the lighter one if you'll be carrying it every day.

l2-128.title: Suggesting it's time to leave.
signature: The last bus leaves in twenty minutes.
Yes. Let's thank our hosts before we head to the stop.

l2-129.title: Opening a meeting on a positive note.
signature: We have two updates today, one good and one difficult.
Let's start with the good news.
The new timetable was approved this morning.

l2-130.title: Disagreeing respectfully on a plan.
signature: I think we should send the new form to everyone at once.
I don't agree with you on this point.
Would you prefer to try it with one team first?

l2-131.title: Clearing up who paid.
signature: Did Sara pay the whole bill before we left?
It was me who paid the bill.
Thanks. I'll send you my share when I get home.

l2-132.title: Checking before leaving the kitchen.
signature: I've washed the last pan. Can we leave now?
See if the gas is turned off.
It's off. I'll switch the light off too.

l2-133.title: Getting oriented in a new city.
signature: Do you already know your way around Boston?
I've never been to Boston before.
Then let's start with the map and mark your hotel.

l2-134.title: Complimenting a homemade dish.
signature: I tried a new recipe for the rice.
Thank you. I added lemon and fresh herbs.

l2-135.title: Asking for a final extension.
signature: How much extra time would make a difference?
All I need is three more days.
All right. Send the draft on Friday so we can review it before Monday.

l2-136.title: Reporting an offer of a taxi.
signature: What did Tom say when he saw you waiting outside?
Tom asked if I needed a taxi.
That was kind of him. Did you take a taxi or wait for the bus?

l2-137.title: Reassuring someone about time.
signature: I still need to check the final slide. How long until we start?
Good. I'll rehearse the ending once before we go in.

l2-138.title: Sorting out a booking error.
signature: My ticket says seat twelve, but this one has a different name on it.
Could you check both tickets before we move anyone?

l2-139.title: Reporting a question about a purchase.
signature: What did Tom ask Mary when she showed him the car?
Tom asked Mary when she had bought her car.
She bought it last month. Tell him she can show it to him tomorrow.

l2-140.title: Finding something you thought was lost.
signature: Did Tom have to call a locksmith after all?
Tom found the keys he thought he had lost.
That's a relief. Where had he left them?

l2-141.title: Making a room bright enough to study.
signature: I'll move the lamp closer to the desk.
Thanks. Now I can see the small print.

l2-142.title: Sorting items for washing.
signature: Shall I put this scarf back in the drawer?
All right. I'll check the label and put it with the other scarves.

l2-143.title: Choosing a place to camp.
signature: How about this flat area beside the path?
This looks like a good spot to set up camp.
Let's check whether camping is allowed here before we unpack.

l2-144.title: Helping someone keep up in class.
signature: Why has Tom stopped volunteering answers in class?
Tom finds it difficult to keep up with the rest of the class.
Let's give him a copy of the questions before the next lesson.

l2-145.title: Giving someone just what they need.
signature: I brought you a phone charger. I remembered yours had stopped working.
This is just what I needed.
Try it here before you go. The cable is in the box.

l2-146.title: Finding material for a project.
signature: I need a book on local history. Where should I look?
There are many books on this subject.
Could you recommend one with pictures and short chapters?

l2-147.title: Deciding where to start reading.
signature: Should we read the introduction or jump straight to the examples?
Let's begin with the first chapter.
Good idea. We'll each bring one question to our next meeting.

l2-148.title: Questioning an offer that sounds suspicious.
signature: The seller wants me to send money before I see the item.
I'll ask to see it first. If they refuse, I'll leave it.

l2-149.title: Deciding whether to wait.
signature: Tom is getting the key. Shall we go to the room now?
Let's wait till he comes back.
Okay. I'll lay out the papers while we're here.

l2-150.title: Checking if the window can be opened.
signature: It's a little stuffy in this room.
Do you mind if I open the window?
Not at all. Open it just a little, please.

l2-151.title: Offering to show someone how.
signature: I haven't used this printer before.
Let me ask you a simple question.
Of course. Do you want to know which size I need?

l2-152.title: Leaving earlier to avoid the rush.
signature: Should we leave at noon or wait until after lunch?
The sooner you leave, the better.
All right. I'll pack lunch so we can leave before noon.

l2-153.title: Reporting a broken door.
signature: Why did you move the meeting to the other room?
One of the doors was broken.
Thanks for letting me know. I'll tell the people who haven't arrived yet.

l2-154.title: Finding a connection at school.
signature: Do you know anyone in the new reading club?
Tom goes to the same school as I do.
Great. Could you ask Tom which room the club uses?

l2-155.title: Writing a first letter in French.
signature: Would you like me to read your letter before you send it?
This is the first time I've ever written a letter in French.
Then let's check the greeting first and keep the rest simple.

l2-156.title: Finishing an outdoor task before the heat.
signature: Shall we move the plants this afternoon?
Let's do this before it gets hot.
You're right. We can move them now and water them later.

l2-157.title: Focusing on today's priorities.
signature: We have a long list of jobs and only two people today.
Let's concentrate on what needs to be done today.
The orders that go out this afternoon should come first.

l2-158.title: Agreeing with one point.
signature: We should try the new schedule with one team before asking everyone to switch.
I agree with you on that point.
Great. Let's ask the morning team to try it next week.

l2-159.title: Relaying a question from reception.
signature: What happened when you got to the front desk?
Tom asked me what I wanted.
Did you tell Tom you had come to collect the key?

l2-160.title: Describing what someone wore.
signature: What did Tom wear to the interview yesterday?
Tom was wearing a gray suit and a red tie.
I might wear my dark blue jacket when I go.

l2-161.title: Offering help for next time.
signature: I stayed late to put all the figures into the spreadsheet.
I could have helped you with your work.
Thanks. I'll ask next time instead of trying to do it all myself.

l2-162.title: Estimating whether someone will come.
signature: Should we keep one more seat free?
It's quite likely that Tom will come.
I'll save one by the door so he can get in easily.

l2-163.title: Describing a way to learn English.
signature: My brother practised short conversations every evening.
This is the way he learned English.
Then I'll try one short conversation after dinner each day.

l2-164.title: Reporting an apology for being late.
signature: What did Tom say when the meeting had already started?
Tom apologized to Mary for being late.
Good. I'll send him the notes from the first ten minutes.

l2-165.title: Making room for extra practice.
signature: We still hesitate when we reach the last two slides.
All we need is a little more practice.
Let's run through those two again before we finish.

l2-166.title: Checking approval before a change.
signature: Did the building manager agree to the new sign?
Let's wait for the reply before we order it.

l2-167.title: Reporting a request to open a window.
signature: Why is the window open when the room is empty?
Tom asked me to open the window.
Could you check whether he still needs it open before we leave?

l2-168.title: Arriving early for good seats.
signature: The show starts at eight, and the seats aren't numbered.
Let's go to the theater early so we can get good seats.
Good idea. We can meet by the theatre at half past seven.

l2-169.title: Passing on a question about a meeting.
signature: Did Tom say why he called while I was at lunch?
Tom wondered when the meeting would start.
Please tell him it starts at two, and send him the link.

l2-170.title: Choosing the best time to visit.
signature: Would it be better to visit Boston in spring or in summer?
This is the best time of year to visit Boston.
Then I'll keep the dates we picked in May.

l2-171.title: Talking about a habit that changed.
signature: Why does Tom bring lunch to work now?
Tom used to eat out every day, but he can't afford to anymore.
Maybe we can swap simple lunch recipes.

l2-172.title: Moving a conversation somewhere quieter.
signature: How was the café for your group meeting?
It was so noisy that we couldn't talk.
Let's try the library meeting room next time.

l2-173.title: Explaining why you left a job.
signature: My shifts changed every week, and I couldn't keep my evening course.
This is why I quit the job.
What kind of schedule would let you keep studying?

l2-174.title: Finding a first step on a hard problem.
signature: Have you tried drawing a diagram for the last question?
I can't figure out how to solve this problem.
Start by drawing the two distances you know. Then label the one you need.

l2-175.title: Checking a bicycle before a ride.
signature: I heard a click when I pushed this bicycle out of the garage.
There's nothing wrong with this bicycle.
Then the sound may have come from the garage door. Let's check.

l2-176.title: Getting useful advice from a colleague.
signature: Did you ask Tom how to handle the calls on your first day?
What was the one thing that helped you most?

l2-177.title: Pointing out an error on a receipt.
signature: The receipt shows three lamps, but I only bought two.
There seems to be a mistake.
I'll check the items and correct the total for you.

l2-178.title: Finding more chances to speak.
signature: How can I hear more natural speech after class?
The best way to learn a language is to live in a country where it's spoken.
I can't travel this year, but I can join a local conversation group.

l2-179.title: Making a formal introduction.
signature: Welcome to the panel. Please take a seat.
Of course. Please tell us your name and the role you're applying for.

l2-180.title: Inviting someone to choose an outfit.
signature: I've put the outfits for the family event in this room.
Thanks. I'll pick something I can also wear to work.

l2-181.title: Reporting a question about the weekend.
signature: Mary mentioned a market but didn't say which town she visited.
Tom wondered where Mary had spent the weekend.
I'll ask her which market it was when I see her.

l2-182.title: Explaining why someone came.
signature: Why did Tom come to the workshop instead of calling?
Tom came here to ask us to help him.
Let's ask him to show us what he needs before we close.

l2-183.title: Planning around morning traffic.
signature: Can we drive across town at eight tomorrow?
There's a lot of traffic here in the mornings.
Then we'll take the train and walk from the station.

l2-184.title: Telling how you became friends.
signature: How did you get to know your friend from Taiwan?
I became friends with him while I was in Taiwan.
Do you still keep in touch now that you live in different places?

l2-185.title: Planning for a late arrival.
signature: Shall we start the reading group as soon as everyone is here?
There's a chance Tom will be late.
Let's start with a short recap. Tom can join the main discussion when he arrives.

l2-186.title: Respecting a donor's privacy.
signature: Should we put the names of the donors on the thank-you board?
The person who donated this money wishes to remain anonymous.
Then we'll write a general thank-you and leave the name off.

l2-187.title: Explaining a simple control.
signature: How do I start printing the labels after I've chosen the size?
All you have to do is push this button.
That's easy. I'll try with one label first.

l2-188.title: Reporting a lunch suggestion.
signature: Why are Tom and Mary looking at that map?
Tom asked Mary where she wanted to go for lunch.
There's a quiet place by the park if they'd like to eat outside.

l2-189.title: Asking for notice before a visit.
signature: I hope to visit you before the end of summer.
Let us know when you'll be coming to Boston.
I'll send you the dates once I've booked the tickets.

l2-190.title: Making a short request with a tag.
signature: The wind is blowing the papers off the desk.
Sure. I'll move the papers away from the window too.

l2-191.title: Encouraging a new learner to ask.
signature: I'm worried I'll ask something everyone already knows.
Don't be afraid to ask questions.
Thanks. Could we go over the first instruction again?

l2-192.title: Reporting an offer to look after a cat.
signature: Who looked after your cat when you travelled?
Tom offered to feed my cat while I was out of town.
That was kind. Would you like to thank him with me?

l2-193.title: Responding to a compliment.
signature: Your explanation made that difficult example much clearer.
It's kind of you to say that.
I mean it. I can work through the next example by myself now.

l2-194.title: Making it just in time.
signature: Did Tom miss his train after getting stuck in traffic?
Tom barely made it in time.
Good. I'll text him the address for when he arrives.

l2-195.title: Reporting a promise about timing.
signature: Should we keep Tom's place on the morning team?
Tom promised Mary that he wouldn't be late.
Then we'll keep him on it and send everyone the start time.

l2-196.title: Taking a discussion over lunch.
signature: We've both got ten minutes until the next meeting.
Good idea. We can use the full lunch break to work out the details.

l2-197.title: Narrowing down a misunderstanding.
signature: I've explained how the first two examples fit the rule.
There's one thing I don't understand.
Which part? Let's compare it with the shorter example.

l2-198.title: Finding who to speak to.
signature: I need to change the delivery address, but I can't do it online.
Tell me who I have to talk to.
Ask for the dispatch desk. They'll check whether the parcel has left.

l2-199.title: Explaining a long wait for the bus.
signature: You sound tired. Are you still at the bus stop?
I've been waiting for the bus for three hours.
I'll check whether another route is running and call you back.

l2-200.title: Keeping a decision open to discussion.
signature: Does the draft mean the new timetable has already been decided?
Good. I'd like to suggest a later start for the evening group.
